items_missed: No agenda statement at the open — he went straight from 'what date are you looking for' into intake. The mid-call 'Let me walk you through how our pricing works then I'll go over your estimate' is a roadmap but carries no 10-15 minute timeframe, so it does not count as an agenda opener.
Never asked 'how are you today?' or any version of it — first words after the greeting were a qualifying question.

Destination access was asserted, not confirmed. The customer's answer was garbled ('it's a second with elevator, second with elevator, and then first is that second elevator and the stop, the stop is third floor. No eight') and Grant said 'I'll get to that here just a second,' then later stated as fact 'that's on the third floor with some stairs to go up.' Third-floor stairs versus an elevator is one of the biggest swing factors in the estimate and it was never nailed down.
Never asked about parking, loading dock, elevator reservation or HOA/COI requirements — on a third-floor apartment-to-apartment move happening the next morning.
Never offered packing services or asked if she needed help packing. He only confirmed the boxes were already done.
No moving-stressor question — never asked what she was worried about, on a same-day-notice move out of a shared apartment.
No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned. 'Insurance' was named once inside the included-items list with zero explanation, and the $2,000 coverage and 60 cents per pound baseline never came up.
Incomplete no-hidden-fees pitch — he covered heavy item fees and stair/elevator fees but skipped credit card fees, transportation fees, fuel surcharge and assembly fees.

Entire Save Your Ass prep speech missing. No 'prep before move day means a shorter move and a lower bill,' no consolidation examples, no take-a-carload tip. This was the single highest-value miss on a next-day move where she is only taking two bedrooms and about six boxes.

Never asked for the booking. She said 'I want to be able to do that cause that work' about the 8:30 slot and he did not close, ending on the passive 'if you want to move forward just give us a call and let us know.'
Never said no deposit is required.
Never mentioned the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email or asked her to reply with corrections.
No final 'any other questions before I let you go?' — he went straight from the 4:30 closing time to 'you have a good one.'
Number of trucks never stated. He said two movers but never named the truck.
Never addressed drive time between the two addresses even though the customer said 'it's like two hours' about the route, which went completely unacknowledged.

Treated 'Yup' as a no-questions answer twice. Both sense-checks ('any questions about any of that information so far?' and 'any questions about that estimate at all') got a one-word reply and he moved on with 'Alrighty, good deal.'
top_strength: The pricing and estimate block was genuinely strong and the best thing on this call. He hit the 'our pricing is super simple' opener verbatim, gave the full rate structure ($102 per hour per mover, two movers, $204 an hour), listed everything included down to pads, wrap, bands and disassembly tools, and delivered all four clock elements cleanly: clock starts when the crew arrives and begins the walkthrough, two and a half hour minimum, then prorated in fifteen minute increments. Then he did something most reps skip: he gave the book range ('anywhere from about four and a half to six hours for two guys'), explained out loud why her move should land under it ('if we're just moving two actual bedrooms maybe some patio items and about six boxes'), and priced three scenarios in dollars ($918, $714, and $510 when she asked about the minimum), always tied back to 'you just pay for the time that we actually work.' The probing that fed it was also solid — he caught the egg chair on the patio, asked walk distance from truck to elevator, and benchmarked boxes against a 25 to 35 range for a two-bedroom.
coaching_note: Grant, the highest-leverage fix is that you built a good quote and then never asked for it. She told you the 8:30 slot worked — 'I want to be able to do that cause that work' — and that was your open door. Say it plainly: 'Great, I have you first appointment at 8:30 tomorrow and there's no deposit required, so I can lock that in right now and get your confirmation email over — want me to go ahead?' You ended on 'if you want to move forward just give us a call,' which hands a next-day, ready-to-book customer back to the market. Second priority is the Save Your Ass speech, which is worth more on this call than almost any other: she moves tomorrow with roughly six boxes, so 'anything that prep you do before we arrive makes the move shorter and your bill lower — consolidate the loose stuff in drawers, take a carload of the small items in your own car, and pull the photos off the walls. Does that make sense?' takes twenty seconds and directly protects the estimate. Third, you left the three differentiators on the table entirely: No Worries $2,000 damage coverage, Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee. You said 'insurance' once inside a list and moved on. LIVE BUSINESS RISKS on this one. (1) Destination access is unresolved. Her answer was garbled and you later stated 'third floor with some stairs' as fact without confirming — if that is actually an elevator building, or actually three flights, the estimate is wrong in one direction or the other, and this goes straight to our estimate accuracy problem. Confirm it before the crew rolls. (2) She said the apartment she is moving out of 'is like 1800' square feet, which is our virtual walkthrough threshold. She is only taking two bedrooms out of a shared unit so a walkthrough may not be warranted, but that judgment call was never made out loud and should be verified before a next-day booking. (3) Expectation gap. She said twice she expects it to take under two hours ('feel pretty be much less than two hours, I don't have much, it's like twin beds') against your 3.5 to 4.5 hour estimate. You reiterated the estimate, which was right, but she never verbally acknowledged it and both of your 'any questions' checks got a one-word 'Yup.' On a move billed hourly, that is a dispute waiting to happen — get the range confirmed in writing and read it back before the crew arrives.
phone_presence_notes: Polite, organized and used her name four times, but mechanical where it counted — he never acknowledged the obvious comprehension difficulty on her side, accepted 'Yup' as a no-questions answer twice, and let her 'it's like two hours' comment pass without a word.
audio_review_reason: The customer's side of the transcript is heavily garbled throughout ('22 bedrooms', 'Jasmine Ono', 'no eight', 'thanks for the work cause I have to take my break two hours'), consistent with either a poor line or a language barrier. Audio is needed to tell whether Grant slowed down, re-confirmed and checked comprehension — which would raise the score — or plowed through a customer who was not following, which would lower it. It also matters for verifying whether the destination floor and stair detail was ever actually confirmed.
